progressiveExplaining.eli5: If you order a meal with a steak that takes 10 minutes and fries that take 1 minute, you don't bring the fries out immediately to get cold. `<Suspense>` is the restaurant kitchen coordinator: it waits until all async dishes are ready, shows a waiting menu (fallback) in the meantime, and serves the whole meal together at the exact same second.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `<Suspense>` is a built-in component that orchestrates nested asynchronous dependencies in the component tree. It provides two slots: `#default` (your async components) and `#fallback` (the loading indicator). An async dependency is any component using top-level `await` in `<script setup>` or loaded via `defineAsyncComponent(() => import('./Child.vue'))`. `<Suspense>` waits for all nested async children to resolve before revealing the tree.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `<Suspense>` creates an asynchronous resolution boundary in the VNode patch pipeline. When an async component mounts, it halts the synchronous render branch and registers a pending promise with the nearest parent `SuspenseContext`. The boundary displays the `#fallback` slot. While fallback is active, all child async operations resolve concurrently. Once all dependencies fulfill, Vue transitions to the `#default` slot and mounts the hydrated DOM tree.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In `@vue/runtime-core`, `SuspenseImpl` manages `deps` (a counter of unresolved asynchronous tasks). When a component with an `async setup()` evaluates, its setup returns a Promise instead of a render function. The renderer flags the instance `Async` and increments `suspense.deps`. Upon Promise settlement, `deps` decrements. When `deps === 0`, `suspense.resolve()` flushes the DOM and triggers `onActivated` / `mounted` lifecycle hooks.

codeComparison.title: Per-Component Loading Spinners vs Coordinated <Suspense>
codeComparison.summary: Multiple independent loading spinners create visual layout thrashing; `<Suspense>` coordinates nested async children into one fallback.

interviewGotchas.question: What qualifies a component as an 'async dependency' that triggers `<Suspense>` in Vue 3?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your understanding of what triggers the Suspense boundary.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: A component is treated as an async dependency by `<Suspense>` if: (1) it uses **top-level `await`** inside `<script setup>`, (2) its `setup()` hook returns a `Promise`, or (3) it is loaded via **`defineAsyncComponent()`**.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: A component that performs data fetching inside `onMounted(async () => ...)` is NOT an async dependency for Suspense because `setup()` finishes synchronously.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you handle errors when an async component inside `<Suspense>` rejects or fails to load?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of error handling alongside Suspense.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Use the **`onErrorCaptured`** lifecycle hook in the parent component or wrap the `<Suspense>` boundary in an Error Boundary component. When an async component fails, `onErrorCaptured` intercepts the error and allows you to set an error state to display a fallback error view.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: `<Suspense>` only manages loading/fallback states; it does *not* catch runtime errors or rejected promises on its own.
